ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Rewrite the constraints respectively as half-planes: 1. x-3y+4≥0, moving terms gives -3y≥-x-4, so y≤(x+4)/3; 2. 3x-y-4≤0, moving terms gives -y≤-3x+4, so y≥3x-4; 3. x+y≥0, so y≥-x. The three boundary lines are y=(x+4)/3, y=3x-4, y=-x. Find the pairwise intersection points: - (x+4)/3=-x, obtaining x=-1, y=1, the intersection point is (-1,1); - 3x-4=-x, obtaining x=1, y=-1, the intersection point is (1,-1); - (x+4)/3=3x-4, obtaining x=2, y=2, the intersection point is (2,2). The feasible region is the triangle enclosed by these three vertices. Because z=3x+2y is a linear function, the maximum value must be attained at a vertex of the feasible polygon. Substitute respectively: z(-1,1)=3×(-1)+2×1=-1; z(1,-1)=3×1+2×(-1)=1; z(2,2)=3×2+2×2=10. Therefore the maximum value is 10.
